title: Engineering Management
blurb: 1:1s, feedback, growth and performance, hiring, team health, planning, DORA metrics, incidents and org design.

quiz.question: Whose meeting is a 1:1?
options: The report's, focused on their topics
quiz.explanation: Report-led 1:1s build trust and surface issues early.

quiz.question: The SBI feedback model stands for…
quiz.explanation: It keeps feedback specific and about observable behaviour.

quiz.question: Which practice predicts interview performance better and reduces bias?
options: Structured interviews with consistent questions and rubrics
quiz.explanation: Structure and rubrics improve validity and fairness.

quiz.question: Which set are the core DORA delivery metrics?
options: Lines of code, commits, story points, bugs
Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, failed deployment recovery time
Velocity, burndown, WIP, cycle time only
quiz.explanation: They measure throughput and stability together.

quiz.question: How should engineering metrics be used?
options: For team and system learning, never individual performance ranking
quiz.explanation: Individual metrics get gamed and damage collaboration.

quiz.question: A team has 72 theoretical engineer-weeks in a quarter. What should you commit?
options: Realistic capacity after leave, on-call and overhead, with allocations for tech health and buffer

quiz.question: What makes a post-incident review blameless?
options: It focuses on systemic contributing factors and improvements, not individual fault
quiz.explanation: People share openly when not blamed, which reveals real causes.

quiz.question: In Team Topologies, which team type provides self-service internal products?
quiz.explanation: Platform teams reduce cognitive load for stream-aligned teams.

problems.title: Missed deadlines
problems.prompt: Your team missed its last three commitments. What do you do?
problems.solution: Diagnose with data and conversations (estimation, scope churn, interrupts, dependencies, debt, CI friction), plan with realistic capacity and buffers, smaller batches and WIP limits, throughput-based forecasts with ranges, early risk communication, explicit stakeholder trade-offs, retros with owned actions.
